result.title: Complementarity without ground truth?
result.summary: Human-AI complementarity captures the idea that a human assisted by an AI system can outperform both the human and the AI acting alone. In prediction tasks, this improvement is assessed against ground truth labels produced through a reference construction procedure and intended to represent the state of affairs to be predicted. Many human-AI interactions, including those where medical AI provides treatment recommendations, however, concern tasks other than predicting what obtains. Their relevant output concerns adequacy relative to a practical goal and depends on several evaluative dimensions. In this work, we examine the ground truth dependence of complementarity and extend it to human-AI interactions where ground truth is not the appropriate reference. We show that tasks beyond prediction can still admit a reference construction procedure that generates adequacy labels. We develop a route for extending complementarity to such settings. It replaces ground truth labels with context-dependent adequacy labels generated through a two-step scoring methodology inspired by multi-criteria decision analysis frameworks in healthcare and it makes the normative choices underlying reference construction explicit. Because the construction of adequacy labels embeds evaluative choices, we draw methodological inspiration from computational reliabilism to identify technical, scientific, and social factors relevant to supporting their construction. Our approach expands the empirical study of human-AI complementarity beyond prediction tasks, enabling its quantitative evaluation in decision-support settings where ground truth is not the appropriate evaluative reference.

AI.brief_summary: 论文论证人机互补性评估不应局限于以 ground truth 为参照的预测任务，提出对治疗建议等决策支持场景用多准则决策分析式的两步评分构造情境依赖的「adequacy labels」，并借 computational reliabilism 显式化其中的规范性选择。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「无唯一正确答案时如何构造评价参照」的思路可能可供核查 LVR 中缺乏标准答案时对 latent 中间状态或人机贡献分配的评估，但完全不涉及 VLM 内部表示与推理状态生成，联系较远。
